dedupe_keys.name: role of spatial variability in liquefaction consequence severity

description: Role of Spatial Variability in Liquefaction Consequence Severity is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "field recon", published or maintained by Armin Stuedlein, Oregon State University (oregonstate.edu). Researchers from Oregon State University conducted geotechnical explorations at select liquefaction case history sites located throughout Christchurch, New Zealand, in order to evaluate the spatial variability of soils at these sites. Coverage: Christchurch and Surrounding Areas. DesignSafe files it as a "field recon" project. Keywords: Cone Penetration Test Data. Published 2021-12-16. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is ODC-By-1.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
